contentFindings.finding: The given single-chromosome bacterial schematic process correctly connects chromosomal copying, distribution and cell separation without nuclear mitosis or a plasmid requirement. This is one narrow causal reproductive-process competence; different real bacterial configurations or universal checkpoint behavior are not inferred from it.

Ordering the fresh four-stage schema and explaining inherited-DNA distribution directly exercises the declared mechanism. Optional1→2→4 is correct under explicitly all-cells-divide/no-death model conditions, and its optional status removes the unsupported population requirement.

The supplied copy-interruption and reversal outcomes require a fresh process explanation and distinguishing cell enlargement from two completed cells. This is a concrete intervention transfer within the same mechanism. The task correctly treats its results as given model data rather than claiming every actual bacterium has this response.

The single required expectation is exercised through process ordering/distribution and a fresh interruption/reversal case. No nonexistent numeric time series, uncontrolled growth law or resource/death-limit performance remains compulsory.
The DE/EN successor expectations, actual case demands and expected performances are equivalent in scope and substantive content.
